deadlines.label: Full Proposal Target Date: September 29, 2025, then the last Monday in September annually; proposals accepted anytime but may miss a panel
deadlines.quote: Full Proposal Target Date(s) : September 29, 2025 Last Monday in September, Annually Thereafter January 26, 2026 Last Monday in January, Annually Thereafter Proposers are highly encouraged to submit by a target date.

deadlines.label: Full Proposal Target Date: January 26, 2026, then the last Monday in January annually; proposals accepted anytime but may miss a panel
deadlines.quote: January 26, 2026 Last Monday in January, Annually Thereafter Proposers are highly encouraged to submit by a target date. Proposals will be accepted anytime, but they may miss a particular panel or committee meeting.

caps.what: total budget, RES designation (up to four years, including any TTE plan)
total budget, EDU designation (up to three years)
total budget, education research focused EDU with cybersecurity and education researcher PI team (extra $100,000)
total budget, SEED designation (up to two years)
optional Transition to Education (TTE) plan, within the RES total budget

match.quote: Cost Sharing Requirements: Inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited.

award.quote: RES projects are limited to $1,200,000 in total budget, with durations of up to four years. Proposals with a total budget of more than $600,000 have additional requirements

sections.name: Project Summary
sections.quote: All RES and SEED proposals must include a prioritized list of 1-6 keywords that describe the general area(s) of the investigation

sections.name: Project Description
sections.quote: Project Description: The project description for proposals submitted to the RES and EDU designations is limited to 15 pages, and 10 pages for the SEED designation.

sections.name: Collaboration Plan
sections.conditional: Projects with more than one PI and a total budget of more than $600,000 (optional otherwise)
sections.quote: all proposals with more than one investigator and a total of more than $600,000 must include a Collaboration Plan of up to 2 pages.

sections.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan
sections.quote: Data Management and Sharing Plan (required): Proposals must include a Supplementary Document of no more than two pages labeled "Data Management and Sharing Plan."

sections.name: Broadening Participation in Computing (BPC) Plan
sections.conditional: Projects with a budget greater than $600,000 that include a computing organization; Standalone up to 3 pages, Connected up to 2 pages plus verified Departmental BPC Plans
sections.quote: Each project with a budget greater than $600,000 and with a lead or non-lead organization (department, school, or institute) that primarily carries out research and education in computer science

sections.name: Transition to Education Plan
sections.quote: Optional TTE Plan for RES proposals: The TTE plan should be labeled as "Transition to Education Plan" and should not exceeding 2 pages.

criteria.name: Intellectual Merit
criteria.quote: Intellectual Merit: The Intellectual Merit criterion encompasses the potential to advance knowledge

criteria.name: Broader Impacts
criteria.quote: Broader Impacts: The Broader Impacts criterion encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.

criteria.name: RES: project scope justifies the level of investment requested
criteria.quote: For all RES projects, reviewers will be asked to evaluate the extent to which the project scope justifies the level of investment requested.

criteria.name: Multi-investigator RES over $600,000: Collaboration Plan synergy and adequate time allocation of key personnel
criteria.quote: For multi-investigator RES projects with a budget greater than $600,000, reviewers will be asked to comment on: the degree to which the Collaboration Plan adequately demonstrates that the participating investigators will work synergistically

criteria.name: RES with TTE Plan: TTE plan meaningfully addresses need, novelty, transition, early adopters, deployment, sustainability and feedback into research
criteria.quote: For RES projects with a TTE Plan, reviewers will be asked to comment on whether the TTE plan meaningfully addresses: the need and novelty of the educational content

criteria.name: BPC Plan meaningfully addresses the five elements
criteria.quote: For projects that are required to include a BPC plan , reviewer will be asked to comment on whether the Broadening Participation in Computing (BPC) plan meaningfully addresses the five elements of a BPC Plan

other: Project Description limited to 10 pages for the SEED designation (15 for RES and EDU)
Title must begin with "SaTC 2.0:" followed by the designation acronym (RES, EDU, SEED, and TTE when used), e.g. SaTC 2.0: RES: TTE: Title; collaborative sets prepend "Collaborative Research:"

RES and SEED: the last paragraph of the Project Summary Overview must be a prioritized list of 1-6 keywords separated by semi-colons; the first keyword must come from the solicitation's topic list (RWR)
Project Personnel and Partner Institutions list must be numbered, one person per line: Full name; Organization(s); Role
Letters of collaboration may be no longer than one page each, with fonts and margins per PAPPG Chapter II.C.2
BPC plan must begin with the heading "Broadening Participation in Computing (BPC) Plan -" followed by Standalone or Connected
No other Supplementary Documents are allowed except as permitted by the PAPPG
Collaborative proposals submitted as separate submissions must be submitted via Research.gov
format.quote: The last paragraph of the Overview section of the Project Summary must consist of a prioritized list of 1-6 keywords, separated by semi-colons. (RWR)

eligibility.item: Eligible organizations: accredited two- and four-year US institutions of higher education (including community colleges) acting on behalf of their faculty, and US non-profit, non-academic organizations directly associated with educational or research activities (independent museums, observatories, research laboratories, professional societies)
eligibility.quote: Proposals may only be submitted by the following: Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs): Two- and four-year IHEs (including community colleges) accredited in, and having a campus located in the U.S., acting on behalf of their faculty members.

eligibility.item: Funding to an international branch campus of a US IHE must be justified (benefit of performing there and why it cannot be done at the US campus)
eligibility.quote: the proposer must explain the benefit(s) to the project of performance at the international branch campus, and justify why the project activities cannot be performed at the US campus.

eligibility.item: PI, co-PI and Senior/Key personnel must hold a tenured/tenure-track position or a primary, full-time, paid research or teaching appointment at a US-based campus of an eligible organization
eligibility.quote: any PI, co-PI, or other Senior/Key project personnel must hold either: a tenured or tenure-track position, or a primary, full-time, paid appointment in a research or teaching position at a US-based campus

eligibility.item: Individuals with primary appointments at for-profit non-academic organizations or overseas branch campuses of US IHEs are not eligible
eligibility.quote: Individuals with primary appointments at for-profit non-academic organizations or at overseas branch campuses of U.S. institutions of higher education are not eligible.

eligibility.item: No more than four proposals per individual (as PI, co-PI or Senior/Key Personnel) in any contiguous 12-month period: two RES, one EDU, one SEED; excess proposals are returned without review
eligibility.quote: During any contiguous 12-month period, an individual may not participate as PI, co-PI, or Senior/Key Personnel in more than four proposals. There is a limit of: two proposals designated as RES; one proposal designated as EDU; and one proposal designated as SEED.

eligibility.item: No limit on the number of proposals per organization
eligibility.quote: Limit on Number of Proposals per Organization: There are no restrictions or limits.

eligibility.item: Sub-awards to overseas campuses/offices of US-based proposing organizations are not permitted
eligibility.quote: Additional Eligibility Info: Sub-awards are not permitted to overseas campuses/offices of US-based proposing organizations.

eligibility.item: Proposals must be submitted under one designation: RES, EDU or SEED
eligibility.quote: Proposals must be submitted pursuant to one of the following designations, each of which may have additional requirements:

eligibility.item: SEED proposals are solicited only through Dear Colleague Letters within specified submission windows (may require concept outlines or specific team composition)
eligibility.quote: The accompanying DCLs will only solicit proposals within specified submission windows and all active DCLs will be listed on the SaTC 2.0 Program web page .

eligibility.item: Proposals focused primarily on design, development or use of offensive techniques are out of scope
eligibility.quote: Proposals that focus primarily on the design, development, or use of offensive techniques are out of scope

eligibility.item: Budget on the Cover Sheet and budget sheets must not exceed the designation maximum or the proposal is returned without review
eligibility.quote: The maximum budget shown on the Cover Sheet and on the budget sheets must not exceed $300,000 for SEED proposals, $1,200,000 for RES proposals (including the budget for the optional TTE plan)

eligibility.item: EDU proposals must include detailed assessment and evaluation plans and must request funds for an evaluator independent of the project
eligibility.quote: All EDU proposals must have detailed plans for assessment and evaluation that are clearly aligned with the project's stated goals based on appropriate metrics.

eligibility.item: Project budgets must include travel for one or more project representatives to attend the SaTC PI meeting
eligibility.quote: Project budgets must include funding for one or more project representatives (PI/co-PI/senior researcher or NSF-approved replacement) to attend the first SaTC PI meeting held after the beginning of the award.

requiredDocuments.item: List of Project Personnel and Partner Institutions (Supplementary Document; lead institution provides for all participants)
requiredDocuments.quote: (required) A list of Project Personnel and Partner Institutions (required. Note: in collaborative proposals, the lead institution should provide this information for all participants)

requiredDocuments.item: Verified Departmental BPC Plans from each institution (for a Connected BPC Plan)
requiredDocuments.quote: up to 2 pages that describe (5) what strategies in the departmental plan the PI and co-PIs will focus on, their specific roles, and their preparation for their work; followed by the verified Departmental BPC Plans from each institution.

requiredDocuments.item: Collaborators and Other Affiliations Information for each participant (Single Copy Document)
requiredDocuments.quote: Single Copy Documents: Collaborators and Other Affiliations Information: Proposers should follow the guidance specified in PAPPG Chapter II.D.2.

requiredDocuments.item: Budget, including travel to the SaTC PI meetings
requiredDocuments.quote: PIs are explicitly required to budget for travel to the PI meetings.
